description: Every new moon, quarter and full moon in a window (or the next few from a date): each with its exact instant, distance, apparent size, supermoon classification under both competing definitions, traditional full-moon name, and any eclipse falling on it. Use for "when is the next full moon" and phase calendars. For the Moon's state right now use astro_moon.

count.description: How many phase events to return from the anchor date.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous result's next_cursor. Send it with the same start/end arguments as the first page.

date.description: Anchor date; the next phases follow it. ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

end.description: Last day of a window. ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, north positive. Send lat and lon together.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, east positive (Lisbon is about -9.14). Send lat and lon together.

phases.description: Optional filter of phase kinds. Omit for all four. Example: ["full_moon"] for full moons only.

place.description: Place name instead of lat/lon, as "City" or "City,CC" with an ISO country code, e.g. "Lisbon,PT". Resolved server-side; the response then carries a required GeoNames CC BY 4.0 credit in its attribution field, which must be preserved when shown.

start.description: First day of a window (use with end). ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

tz.description: IANA timezone like "Europe/Lisbon" to render event times in local time. Optional; a resolved place supplies its own timezone.

name: astro_moon_phases

outputSchema.description: The MCP projection of a CycleCalcs v2 response: the answer, plus the provenance a caller needs to use it honestly.

attribution.description: The credit line to display verbatim when rights is attribution_required.

data.description: New, first quarter, full and last quarter moons in a date range.

phase_count.description: How many phases fall in the window.

phases.description: Each phase with its exact instant and name.

summary.description: A one-line reading of the range.

next_cursor.description: Present only when more rows exist. Send it back with the SAME start/end arguments as the first call to get the next page.

not_computed.description: Data this API deliberately does not serve, and why. Present only when the question touched such a field. An absence named here is information: treat it as "withheld", never as "none exists".

rights.description: Either unrestricted, or attribution_required when third-party place data was used. When attribution_required, the attribution line must be shown.

warnings.description: Machine-readable notices about this answer. Present only when non-empty. Never changes whether the call succeeded.

title: Lunar phase calendar
